comments.value: Agreed, I'm sick of having to choose between 100 material slot 50 skinned mesh renderer avatars being shown and having that one guy with a 70,001 poly avatar that's perfectly optimized otherwise being hidden and seeing everyone as a fallback as a result.

Yes. It's so frustrating to have to hide or show everything via "show avatar". Even if i can specify "hide lights" or "hide animations" *per person* that's still more powerful than "make everyone except friends + 'shown avatars' go to fallback." (Especially because in 80 person lobbies, friends often change avatars once or twice so I'd rather the safety settings auto hide individual components on them based on performance, rather than being locked into "show avatar")

Also, add avatar download size and performance rank in the Safety Settings for each Trust Rank. Every time I'm in the mood to tolerate lower FPS for more immersion I have to change the download size in the large menu settings (which means more extra steps). I want to download my Friends 150mb avatar without having to show them individually one by one.

I want to show Very Poor Avatars to my Friends and Trust Rank and show avatars for Lower Ranks but only if they are not Very Poor.

tbh I see no much sense in the ranks at all.

For years from sep 2018 when those ranks were added I never understood how purple "trusted users" are more trusted than regular green users or something in terms of performance. They all roughly the same.

In terms of content too. I only seen disturbing content from some visitors/new users but green Users and higher also roughly the same and rarely do shit, but if do both equally.

@{5a9fe9983955314156acc4f7|full_name} I think it's a holdover from when avatar performance was a trusted thing, because of how many people would abuse avatars to spam shaders or whatever in public instances. It was much more of a wild west and we didn't have the personal controls that we do now.

details:
This feature request is asking for:

**The ability for users to set safety settings based on specific avatar stats, rather than the current broad "shaders", "custom animations", etc.**

So for example: Being able to ignore lights and polygons for very poor avatars, but being able to restrict Texture Memory or Skinned Meshes to Poor or Medium.

This allows users to tailor their expeirences more to their hardware and what they feel is acceptable in terms of performance.

Bonus points for a "presets" system. The safety settings themselves could be converted to this system, where VRChat has presets for each trust level, and users can make custom presets for each trust level or globally.
title: Granular Safety Settings
